text: {"memo": "Walmart’s FY2024, ended January 31, 2025, showed resilient retail execution. Revenue rose 3.9% to about $648 billion, up from $605 billion in FY2023. Net income increased to about $7.2 billion from $5.8 billion in FY2023, while diluted EPS was about $2.65 versus $2.04 in FY2023. Gross margin remained under pressure, around 32.5%, and net margin about 1.1%, reflecting freight and wage costs, though Walmart’s operating margin improved. Comparable sales grew 2.4% in FY2024, versus 7.3% in FY2023 and 6.7% in FY2022. Revenue growth was slower in FY2024 but still positive; FY2023 revenue was up 5.7% from $572 billion in FY2022, and FY2022 net income was $6.8 billion versus $5.7 billion in FY2021. Cash flow remained strong, with operating cash flow around $36 billion in FY2024 and free cash flow above $20 billion after capex. The prior fiscal years showed recovery from pandemic-era demand: FY2021 revenue was $480 billion, net income $6.7 billion, EPS $2.28; FY2020 revenue $432 billion, net income $4.1 billion, EPS $1.88. The business kept gaining market share and controlling costs, but margin recovery was gradual. View: WMT shares look supported into 2025, though valuation and softer consumer backdrop warrant a premium multiple."}
